_note: SAMPLE DATA for the LeaseCheck demo. These are plain-language summaries, not legal advice, and may be incomplete or out of date. CU Boulder Student Legal Services must review them before LeaseCheck is used with students.

rules.title: Security deposit return
rules.summary: In Colorado, a landlord must return the security deposit with an itemized list of deductions within one month after the lease ends. The lease can extend this to no more than 60 days. Normal wear and tear cannot be deducted.
red_flags: Return deadline longer than 60 days
Deposit labeled non-refundable
Automatic deductions (cleaning, painting, re-keying) charged no matter the unit's condition
No deadline stated at all

rules.title: Late fees
rules.summary: In Colorado, a landlord cannot charge a late fee until rent is at least 7 days late. The fee cannot be more than $50 or 5% of the past-due rent, whichever is greater. A landlord cannot evict a tenant only for unpaid late fees.
red_flags: Late fee charged before day 8
Fee above the greater of $50 or 5% of past-due rent
Daily or escalating late fees
Eviction threatened for unpaid late fees alone

rules.title: Move-in and recurring fees
rules.summary: Fees on top of rent should be clearly listed with amounts. Colorado has added limits on some rental fees in recent years, and the rules change often. Students should ask what each fee pays for, whether it is refundable, and how much they will pay in total each month.
red_flags: Fees with no stated amount
Fees set by the landlord 'as determined'
Large non-refundable administrative or move-in fees
Per-person monthly fees that add a lot to the real rent
Flat utility charges that don't depend on usage
rules.source: General guidance; verify current Colorado fee laws

rules.title: Ending the lease early
rules.summary: No Colorado law sets a standard lease-break fee. Colorado courts have generally said landlords must make reasonable efforts to re-rent the unit instead of charging the full remaining rent. Some tenants have special early-termination rights, for example survivors of domestic violence and military members.
red_flags: All remaining rent due at once (acceleration)
Lease-break fee above about 2 months' rent
Both a large fee and rent until re-rented
No subletting or replacement-tenant option
rules.source: Colorado case law on mitigation; C.R.S. 38-12-402 (summary)

rules.title: Repairs and habitability
rules.summary: Colorado's warranty of habitability requires landlords to keep rentals safe and livable, including heat, water, plumbing, electricity and freedom from serious pests or mold. Tenants cannot waive this right in a lease. Tenants can be charged for damage they cause.
red_flags: Tenant accepts the unit 'as-is' and waives habitability claims
Tenant responsible for all repairs regardless of cause
Tenant responsible for major systems (roof, heating, plumbing)

rules.title: Landlord entry
rules.summary: Colorado has no single statute setting a notice period for landlord entry, but a standard lease promises reasonable notice (commonly 24 hours) except in emergencies, and entry for legitimate reasons only.
red_flags: Entry at any time without notice
Entry for 'any purpose'

rules.title: Liability waivers and attorney fees
rules.summary: Clauses that release the landlord from liability for its own negligence, or that make only the tenant pay attorney fees whatever the outcome, are one-sided and may not be enforceable. Clauses where the prevailing party recovers fees are common.
red_flags: Tenant releases landlord from liability for the landlord's own negligence
Tenant pays landlord's attorney fees regardless of outcome
Jury trial waiver
Landlord can change lease terms by posting notice

rules.title: Joint and several liability
rules.summary: Joint and several liability means each roommate can be held responsible for the whole rent and all damages, not just their share. It is legal and common in Boulder student leases, but it matters more when there are many roommates.
red_flags: Joint liability combined with many tenants
Joint liability plus no subletting or replacement option

rules.title: Boulder occupancy limits
rules.summary: Colorado HB24-1007 (2024) stops cities from limiting how many unrelated people can live together. Boulder has stopped enforcing its old 3-or-4 unrelated person limits. Occupancy can still be limited for health and safety reasons, such as building and fire codes, bedroom size, emergency exits (egress) from bedrooms, and the property's rental license.
red_flags: More than about 2 people per bedroom
People sleeping in rooms that aren't legal bedrooms (e.g. basements without egress windows)
Lease asks tenants to hide or misstate how many people live there
Lease cites outdated unrelated-person limits or penalizes tenants for them
Very strict guest limits with large fines
rules.source: HB24-1007; City of Boulder occupancy page (summary)

rules.title: Boulder rental license
rules.summary: Long-term rentals in the City of Boulder must have a rental license, which includes safety inspections. Students can ask the landlord for the license number and look it up with the City of Boulder.
red_flags: Landlord refuses to state the license
Lease says the owner makes no representation about licensing
